title: Safeguard Presets and Preemption Matrix for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Lucas Martinez
description: PRD for a set of operator-facing 'Safeguard Presets' and a formal 'Preemption Matrix' that together provide predictable tenant QoS on Dedicated pools. Presets allow tenants and operators to choose a safe default for reservation behavior (conservative/balanced/aggressive) and control burst tokens, headroom, and preemption sensitivity. The Preemption Matrix formalizes how eviction, throttling, and fallback occur across isolation classes and hardware zones to minimize noisy-neighbor impact and ensure graceful degradation.
goals: Provide three operational presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) that configure reserve fractions, burst budgets, and autoscale headroom
Define a deterministic Preemption Matrix mapping isolation class x capacity state -> action (evict, soft-throttle, route-to-hosted, queue)
Enable tenant-level opt-in for presets with safe defaults and cross-tenant fairness enforcement
Surface clear telemetry and SLO regressions tied to preset changes for post-rollout validation
non_goals: Implementing a new global matchmaking/routing algorithm (out of scope)
Replacing existing billing model or per-token charge logic
Changing supported deployment modes (this only affects Dedicated capacity)
success_metrics: <20% increase in tail latency incidents attributable to eviction after rollout (measured over 30d)
Reduce emergency preemption events for P2/P3 tenants by 40% in conservative preset
>90% operator satisfaction in limited beta (survey) for configuration comprehensibility
Telemetry coverage: preset usage and preemption events instrumented for 100% of Dedicated pools
acceptance_criteria: API: tenants can set preset on their reservation via PUT /dedicated/reservations/{id} with preset: conservative|balanced|aggressive and receive 200
Backend: preset translates into enforced parameters: reserve_fraction, burst_budget_tokens, autoscale_headroom, preemption_policy_id
Preemption Matrix: table implemented in orchestration service and deterministically applied during capacity contention; manifests logged
Behavioral: when a tenant switches from aggressive -> conservative, system enforces reduced burst budget immediately without violating existing reservations
Observability: dashboards show per-preset breakdown, preemption counts by reason, time series for queueing and evictions
Rollout: feature gated by 'presets' flag and can be disabled without data loss; canary rollout to 10% of clusters first
Integration tests: end-to-end test that simulates surge and validates actions in preemption matrix for all isolation classes
Docs: console help text and API docs updated with examples and recommended presets for common workloads
api_surface: 1) PUT /dedicated/reservations/{id} {preset: string, custom_overrides: optional map-as-json-string} 2) GET /dedicated/reservations/{id} returns computed enforcement params 3) Admin GET /dedicated/preemption-matrix returns current matrix and rationales
ui_changes: Console: Reservation Edit modal adds 'Safeguard preset' dropdown with inline help; a per-pool table shows active presets and predicted burst headroom. Rollout controls for operators to toggle 'presets' feature flag per zone.
telemetry: Emit events: preset_change, preemption_event(reason, action, affected_reservations), burst_budget_exhausted, autoscale_headroom_trigger. Tag all events with reservation_id, team_id, isolation_class, pool_zone. Add Grafana dashboards and an alert rule 'preemption-spike' tied to 5x baseline preemption rate.
notes: Design review 2026-03-05: UX requested in-line examples showing token consumption over 1h to explain burst_budget
Trade-off: conservative preset reduces emergency preemption but increases per-tenant cost due to higher reserved fraction
Ops ask: ability to override preset at pool level for critical tenants; included as admin override in scope
Implementation approach recommended: implement presets as configuration profiles that map to existing autoscale and eviction primitives to minimize runtime changes
rollout_plan: 1) Implement backend + API behind feature flag. 2) Internal dogfood on staging for 2 weeks with synthetic surge tests. 3) Canary on 10% of clusters for 7 days; monitor preemption, latency, and cost signals. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% across regions if no regressions. 5) Post-rollout review and tweak preset parameters.
risks_mitigation: Risk: aggressive preset may lead to noisy neighbor regressions. Mitigation: limit aggressive preset availability to tenants with explicit justification and add a circuit-breaker that disables aggressive preset in a pool when preemption rate exceeds threshold.
